subject.title: Feature: Per-agent plugin configuration overrides for multi-agent setups

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic `agents.list[].plugins` override contract for plugin config, and what precedence, SecretRef, validation, lifecycle, and doctor semantics should it use?
rationale: The request would let different agents use different plugin credentials and state boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security and compatibility contract from source evidence alone.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a shared core/plugin SDK contract for per-agent plugin config with explicit merge precedence, SecretRef handling, schema validation, restart semantics, and migration/docs coverage.

options.title: Keep config global and solve narrower plugins
options.body: Leave `plugins.entries` global and handle memory/wiki/provider needs through plugin-owned agent maps or dedicated plugin settings, reducing core surface but fragmenting operator UX.

options.title: Defer to per-agent plugin installation
options.body: Treat independent installs as the isolation boundary and route this issue behind the per-agent install design, trading config simplicity for a larger lifecycle/install change.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a shared core/plugin SDK contract for per-agent plugin config with explicit merge precedence, SecretRef handling, schema validation, restart semantics, and migration/docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin config runtime, current config schema, and security-sensitive extension contracts where recent history and CODEOWNERS context point most strongly to this owner.
